inspection_summary: Whole-source inspection found a coherent asymptotic-analysis article that constructs an incomplete-gamma-smoothed zeta expansion by Mellin-contour methods, derives a critical-strip remainder bound through scaled gamma-ratio monotonicity, specializes the construction to exponential and complementary-error-function smoothing, and shows why simple smoothing forces a Gram-type O(t) cutoff rather than a Riemann-Siegel-type O(sqrt(t)) cutoff. Numerical evidence exposes both parameter tradeoffs and the loss of sharpness of the proved remainder bound near optimal truncation. Appendices establish the relation to the earlier symmetric expansion and the monotonicity facts used in the bound. The prose preserves the mechanisms, but many displayed formulas are degraded by extraction and require scan verification before exact symbolic reuse.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic metadata and a source-level summary of exponential smoothing, critical-strip scope, O(|t|) cutoff, and numerical validation.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Compares Gram, Riemann-Siegel, and smoothed formulas; identifies cutoff scale, smoothing shape, discontinuity removal, and the paper's simple-smoothing-versus-efficiency tradeoff.

sections_inspected.label: 2. A generalised expansion for zeta(s)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds the incomplete-gamma-smoothed representation from a Mellin/Perron integral, contour displacement, residues, and the zeta functional relation, then states its computational admissibility condition and special case.

sections_inspected.label: 3. A bound on R_M when a > 0
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reduces the remainder integral to gamma-ratio estimates, uses monotonicity and incomplete-gamma bounds, and diagnoses the parameter range in which the bound coefficient remains moderate.

sections_inspected.label: 4. An exponentially-smoothed main sum
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Specializes to exponential smoothing, derives the forced Gram-scale cutoff and optimal truncation, analyzes the free smoothing parameter, and compares actual numerical error with the rigorous remainder bound.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Concluding remarks
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Contrasts the complementary-error-function specialization with Berry-Keating smoothing, identifies a possible transition in the free parameter, and isolates the non-sharp remainder analysis as the main unresolved bottleneck.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix A. Relation between expansions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Shows that a parameter specialization, pole cancellation by trivial zeros, analytic continuation, and a scale choice recover the earlier convergent critical-line expansion.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix B. Monotonicity of F and G
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Proves evenness and monotonicity of an unscaled gamma ratio and a sufficient monotone-decrease regime for its scaled form, supporting the remainder estimate.

sections_inspected.label: References and affiliation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliography, page furniture, and author affiliation; no independent semantic unit.

accepted_units.title: Gram and Riemann-Siegel formulas separate by cutoff scale
accepted_units.why_material: The paper frames computational strength through the number of retained Dirichlet terms: Euler-Maclaurin asymptotics force a Gram-scale O(|t|) main sum, while the Riemann-Siegel formula uses about O(sqrt(t)) terms. This supplies the baseline criterion later used to classify smoothed expansions.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the asymptotic-character condition on the Gram truncation and the critical-line efficiency comparison; exact displayed formulas are not needed for the qualitative cutoff claim.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on asymptotic-order and cutoff notation; the prose is recoverable, but scan verification is required for exact formulas (1.1)-(1.2).

accepted_units.title: Complementary-error smoothing removes the discrete-cutoff discontinuity
accepted_units.why_material: Two convergent/smoothed representations replace the sharp Riemann-Siegel upper limit by a complementary-error transition that is near one below the cutoff and decays above it. The text explicitly connects smoothing to continuity in t while retaining the Riemann-Siegel-scale cutoff.
accepted_units.context_note: The Berry-Keating and incomplete-gamma examples are compared only at the level established here: both smooth the cutoff and retain roughly the same term scale, though their error-function arguments differ.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the error-function interpretation of incomplete-gamma asymptotics and on N_t notation; scan verification is required for exact equations (1.3)-(1.4).

accepted_units.title: Simple smoothing forces a less efficient Gram-type cutoff
accepted_units.why_material: This is the paper's governing negative result: although a free parameter permits exponential or real-error-function smoothing, asymptotic correction and remainder terms force the transition to occur after O(t) terms. It separates aesthetic simplicity of the smoothing rule from computational efficiency.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a programmatic claim proved and illustrated in later sections, not an independent theorem with all hypotheses in this span.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-level asymptotic classification is intact; interpreting constants or exact parameter regimes requires the later formulas.

accepted_units.title: Mellin-Perron construction of an incomplete-gamma-smoothed Dirichlet sum
accepted_units.why_material: A Mellin integral for the incomplete gamma function is inserted into an absolutely convergent sum, summation and integration are reversed, and contour displacement across the poles at zero and 1-s produces the basic smoothed zeta representation. This is the analytic bridge from a smoothing kernel to zeta.
accepted_units.context_note: The pole-separation restriction is presented for 0 < sigma < 1 and is said to extend to sigma > 1 by contour indentation except at a stated double-pole configuration.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula- and contour-dependent; the prose recovers the construction, pole locations, and justification, but scan verification is required for exact equations (2.1)-(2.3) and parameter inequalities.

accepted_units.title: Contour shifting yields the generalized expansion and its computational admissibility condition
accepted_units.why_material: Moving the remainder contour across gamma poles and applying the zeta functional relation yields a finite correction series plus a remainder, which combines with the smoothed main sum into the generalized expansion. The coefficients unusually contain zeta itself, so usefulness requires a parameter regime in which those zeta values are computable by a convergent Dirichlet series; the earlier formula appears as a special case.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact coefficients and remainder contour are present but extraction-damaged. Line 206 is needed to retain the explicit Appendix A connection omitted by the v1 endpoint.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires the functional equation, residue expansion, and displayed coefficient formulas; scan verification is required before exact symbolic use of (2.4)-(2.8).

accepted_units.title: The remainder is reduced to a weighted gamma-ratio integral
accepted_units.why_material: After fixing the remainder contour and applying the zeta functional relation, elementary gamma/hyperbolic estimates reduce |R_M| to an integral governed by a gamma-function ratio F. The appendix-supplied facts that F is even and increasing, while its scaled form G decreases in the relevant regime, create the monotone structure needed for a usable bound.
accepted_units.context_note: The paper assumes critical-strip s, positive real parameters, p > 1, and the admissibility inequality inherited from Section 2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The reduction is highly equation-dependent and several displays are degraded; checked prose preserves the bounding strategy, but scan verification is required for (3.1)-(3.2) and the preceding integral.

accepted_units.title: Monotonicity turns the remainder integral into an incomplete-gamma bound
accepted_units.why_material: The integral is split at t, monotonic bounds on the scaled gamma ratio control the tails, and the remaining integral is evaluated as an incomplete gamma function. A standard incomplete-gamma inequality then gives a simpler explicit estimate when X exceeds N.
accepted_units.context_note: This span supplies the reusable inequality mechanism between the definition of F/G and the final remainder bound, rather than merely routine algebra.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on split-integral, scaled-gamma, and incomplete-gamma notation; exact constants and powers in (3.3)-(3.7) require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The final bound has a coefficient that loses moderate size beyond an M-scale
accepted_units.why_material: The derived critical-strip bound isolates a computable coefficient G_p(M;t). The reported values agree with its fixed-M asymptotic behavior at low M but show that it ceases to be order one once M exceeds an approximate (t/2)^(2/3)/p scale, foreshadowing why the bound deteriorates well before optimal truncation.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 303-314 complete the sentence and table interpretation severed by the v1 endpoint at line 298.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The qualitative growth regime is clear in prose and Table 1; the exact bound (3.8), exponent formatting, and tabulated symbols require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Exponential smoothing inherits a forced Gram-scale cutoff
accepted_units.why_material: Choosing a=1 converts the incomplete-gamma kernel to a real exponential and integer p simplifies the correction coefficients. Large-order behavior of those corrections imposes K > t/(2 pi), so the nominal switch-off near n approximately K necessarily retains O(t) terms and the formula is Gram-type.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the principal specialization of the general construction and directly establishes the advertised smoothing-versus-efficiency tradeoff.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the exponential kernel, coefficient sequence, and asymptotic-character criterion; scan verification is required for exact equations (4.1)-(4.3).

accepted_units.title: Optimal truncation and sharper smoothing pull accuracy in opposite directions
accepted_units.why_material: The correction series initially decreases and then diverges, with an estimated optimal index depending sensitively on p and the scale ratio. Increasing p suppresses the main-sum tail and makes shifted zeta values easier, but eventually destroys asymptotic character and raises the least correction term, limiting attainable accuracy.
accepted_units.context_note: The tradeoff is conditional on t/(2p) being large and on K chosen at Gram scale.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose fully states the qualitative tradeoff; the precise optimal-truncation law (4.4) requires scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Critical-line specialization separates optimal from practically sufficient truncation
accepted_units.why_material: For p=1 and K=t/(2 pi), the paper specializes the expansion and remainder bound on the critical line, then shows numerically that optimal truncation can be enormous while much smaller, deliberately suboptimal truncations already deliver high accuracy for larger t. The t=10 case also shows that optimal truncation need not imply uniformly spectacular accuracy at modest height.
accepted_units.context_note: Tables 2-3 support a truncation-strategy claim rather than serving as standalone numerical training material.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the critical-line phase and exact expansion (4.5); numeric conclusions are readable, but exact formulas, exponents, and table values require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The rigorous remainder bound is realistic only far below optimal truncation
accepted_units.why_material: Direct comparison of actual Z(t) error with the proved bound shows close tracking for modest M, followed by rapid deterioration around M proportional to t and uselessness at optimal truncation. This distinguishes true expansion accuracy from sharpness of the available proof technique.
accepted_units.context_note: The source attributes the failure to the bound rather than using it to refute the expansion's asymptotic nature.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Relies on Table 4 and the prose interpretation; scan verification is required for exact scientific-notation entries and the precise bracketed threshold.

accepted_units.title: Increasing K buys accuracy with more main-sum work, while increasing p can reduce accuracy
accepted_units.why_material: The controlled computation separates two knobs: increasing K raises attainable accuracy at the cost of moving the effective cutoff outward, whereas increasing p sharpens exponential tail decay but lowers the optimal correction-series truncation and worsens its least term. This is a concrete multi-objective design constraint.
accepted_units.context_note: The comparison is demonstrated at t=100 with the correction sum capped as stated in Table 5, so it should not be generalized beyond the tested regime without new evidence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The qualitative comparison is explicit in prose; exact errors and parameter settings in Table 5 require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Complementary-error-function smoothing is simple but remains Gram-type
accepted_units.why_material: Selecting a=1/2 changes the kernel from an exponential to erfc while leaving the correction-series asymptotic constraint intact. With p=1 on the critical line, K must again be of order t/(2 pi), so changing the simple smoothing function alone does not recover Riemann-Siegel efficiency.
accepted_units.context_note: This provides a controlled sibling representation to the a=1 specialization rather than a new general expansion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on Q(1/2,z^2)=erfc(z) and the displayed critical-line expansion; exact equations (5.1)-(5.2) require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The argument geometry of the smoothing kernel controls the cutoff class
accepted_units.why_material: The Berry-Keating error-function argument depends logarithmically on n/N_t and cuts off at Riemann-Siegel scale, whereas the paper's fixed-order incomplete-gamma choices yield Gram scale. The contrast motivates the proposed transition study between a=O(1) and the s-dependent choice a=s/2.
accepted_units.context_note: The transition domain is posed as an open direction, not established by the source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on comparing how n enters two error-function arguments and how a scales with s; exact cutoff notation is extraction-degraded but the prose comparison is intact.

accepted_units.title: Crude absolute bounds conceal possible optimal-truncation accuracy
accepted_units.why_material: The paper identifies the failure of its remainder estimate past moderate M as an artifact of crude inequalities and proposes analysis that retains integrand oscillation. It carefully separates an unproved assumption of asymptoticity from numerical indications of potentially enormous accuracy at optimal truncation.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a limitation and research direction; it does not establish the conjectured asymptotic behavior.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded; its quantitative reference to Table 2 inherits that table's scan-verification requirement.

accepted_units.title: Trivial-zero cancellation transforms the generalized formula into its symmetric special case
accepted_units.why_material: Setting a=s/2 and p=1 leaves a single contour pole because other gamma poles cancel against zeta's trivial zeros. After the functional equation and a variable reversal, the residual integral matches the original Mellin form with transformed s and reciprocal scale, revealing a dual smoothed sum.
accepted_units.context_note: This explains structurally, rather than merely asserts, how the generalized construction contains the earlier formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly contour- and formula-dependent; the cancellation and transformation are clear in prose, but exact equations (A.1)-(A.3) require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Absolute convergence and analytic continuation recover the critical-line expansion
accepted_units.why_material: The two-sum expansion is first justified in an angular domain by incomplete-gamma decay, extended by analytic continuation, and then specialized through a scale choice and conjugacy to obtain the earlier convergent formula on the critical line.
accepted_units.context_note: This closes the Appendix A equivalence argument; the omitted/degraded display just before line 575 must be checked in the scan for exact reconstruction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on incomplete-gamma sectorial asymptotics, analytic continuation, conjugacy, and a precise K choice; scan verification is required for (A.4) and the scale normalization.

accepted_units.title: A gamma-function ratio is even and increasing above a parameter threshold
accepted_units.why_material: A product representation makes F even, and logarithmic differentiation expresses its derivative with a sign that is positive for x>0 when the parameter exceeds one half. This supplies the monotonicity invoked when bounding the remainder integral.
accepted_units.context_note: The boundary case F=1 at a=1/2 is recorded and helps delimit the lemma.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on a gamma-ratio product and derivative series; the sign argument is recoverable from prose, but exact formulas (B.1)-(B.2) require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Scaling removes gamma-ratio growth and exposes the eventual monotonic sign
accepted_units.why_material: The dominant power growth of F is factored out to define G tending to one. Its large-x expansion identifies a parameter regime with eventual decrease and records a closed boundary-case expression, providing the normalization used throughout the remainder analysis.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit gives asymptotic, not global, monotonicity; the global sufficient condition is established in the following unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on gamma-ratio asymptotics and exact coefficient signs; scan verification is required for (B.3)-(B.4), whose symbols are degraded.

accepted_units.title: An integral-sign argument proves global decrease of the scaled gamma ratio
accepted_units.why_material: A gamma identity and product representation convert the logarithmic derivative of G into integral expressions. Two integrations by parts reduce its sign to positivity of a sine transform of a positive decreasing function, proving G decreases for x>0 when a>1; numerical computation suggests a lower threshold but is explicitly separate from the proof.
accepted_units.context_note: The source omits details for the sign properties of H and labels the approximately 0.63605 threshold as direct Mathematica evidence, so only a>1 is analytically established here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly dependent on formulas (B.5)-(B.6), the definition of H, and a sine-transform positivity fact; scan verification is required before exact proof transcription.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Smoothing geometry, not smoothness alone, determines computational class
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Both exponential and erfc kernels can remove a sharp cutoff, yet fixed-order simple kernels remain Gram-type because their correction asymptotics force K=O(t); a logarithmic or s-dependent kernel geometry can instead retain the Riemann-Siegel O(sqrt(t)) transition.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source demonstrates selected fixed-order and s/2 choices and explicitly leaves the intervening a-domain unexplored, so it does not establish a general classification theorem.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Tail suppression competes with correction-series fertility
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A parameter that makes the smoothed main sum decay faster can simultaneously shorten or degrade the useful asymptotic correction series, while enlarging the scale K improves accuracy only by increasing main-sum work; useful tuning must balance both series rather than optimize the smoother alone.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The numerical comparison is restricted to the source's stated critical-line parameter choices and capped truncations.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Monotone majorants enable certification but can erase oscillatory accuracy
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Scaling a gamma ratio and proving monotonicity makes an explicit remainder certificate possible, but the absolute monotone majorization discards oscillation and produces a coefficient that grows too early, explaining why the rigorous bound can be realistic for practical truncations yet useless near optimal truncation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source proposes oscillation-aware refinement but neither supplies it nor proves asymptoticity at optimal truncation.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The generalized expansion contains a symmetric critical-line representation through parameter duality
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The a=s/2 specialization triggers trivial-zero cancellation and a transformed Mellin integral, producing dual incomplete-gamma sums whose analytic continuation and scale choice recover the earlier convergent critical-line formula.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Exact symbolic identities and scale constants are extraction-sensitive and must be verified against the page scan before reuse.
